name: Crimpshrine
label: Lookout!
lede: Two kids started a band at 12 and 13 with one drum and a three-string guitar, and seven years later they were the sound of Berkeley's Gilman Street.

eras.title: S.A.G.: one drum, three strings
eras.text: Aaron Cometbus and Jesse Michaels started a band as teenagers with almost no gear. Jeff Ott joined at 12 and the band that became Crimpshrine grew from there.

years.h: S.A.G. forms with one drum and a three-string guitar
years.p: [[Aaron Cometbus|47e0c017-6e9e-408b-8c9e-e01950fb4892]] (13) and [[Jesse Michaels|cf8b6e69-523c-4a64-b2e8-c64f171b742b]] (13) start S.A.G. in the East Bay; Jeff Ott joins at 12 on drums, later swapping to guitar as Cometbus takes over drums.
years.xp:
According to Wikipedia, the band's first setup was a single drum and a guitar with three strings tuned to a barre chord. Michaels later fronted [[Operation Ivy|931e1d1f-6b2f-4ff8-9f70-aa537210cd46]].

Ott and Cometbus would stay together for the next seven years.

years.p: After Jesse Michaels quits, Jeff Ott and Aaron Cometbus rename the band, taking the name from a nickname for a girl they knew with bleached, burned, crimped hair.
years.xp: Wikipedia says Michaels left citing his own heavy marijuana use. Ott took over lead vocals and also played synthesizer and piano in this period.

eras.title: A basement and a bass player
eras.text: The band spent years rehearsing in Ott's basement with a shifting cast before a stable lineup and first recordings arrived.

years.h: Tim Armstrong, then called Lint, plays bass
years.p: During a revolving-door year, future [[Rancid|24f8d8a5-269b-475c-a1cb-792990b0b2ee]] and Operation Ivy guitarist [[Tim Armstrong|beaecc2d-20c7-4221-8fd2-682c82f0faab]] fills in on bass for Crimpshrine.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists Armstrong, then known as Lint, among the musicians who cycled through the band in 1985.

years.p: Bassist Pete Rypins locks in the trio of Ott, Cometbus and Rypins, and the band starts playing out.

years.h: First demo recorded at 924 Gilman Street
years.p: Crimpshrine tape their first demo at the all-ages East Bay club where the scene was forming.
years.xp: Per Wikipedia, the demo was recorded at 924 Gilman Street in Berkeley.

years.h: Two songs for the Turn It Around! comp
years.p: Crimpshrine record "Another Day" and "Rearranged" for the Maximumrocknroll compilation Turn It Around!

years.h: Recording Sleep, What's That? at Dangerous Rhythm
years.p: The band cut their debut EP in Oakland at Dangerous Rhythm Studios. The title track was inspired by Berkeley's 1987 Reaganville tent city protest.
years.xp: Per Wikipedia, "In My Mind" was written after Ott saw a bus driver's callous response to an unresponsive Black passenger, a scene he took as unconscious racism.

eras.title: Lookout! and a stranded tour
eras.text: The debut EP put Crimpshrine on Lookout Records and the East Bay map. Then their only US tour fell apart in Florida.

years.h: Sleep, What's That? comes out on Lookout Records
years.p: The EP arrives January 30, 1988 as Lookout LK 004, 2,000 numbered copies with red stamps.
years.xp: According to Wikipedia, a pressing plant mistake put about 50 copies on blue marble vinyl. Later pressings updated the cover and booklet colors after Lookout relocated to Berkeley in 1991.

years.h: Idon Bryant adds a second guitar
years.p: Idon Bryant joins, making Crimpshrine a four-piece for the first time.

years.h: Bandmates walk out in Gainesville, Florida
years.p: On Crimpshrine's only US tour, Pete Rypins and Idon Bryant abruptly quit in Gainesville, leaving Ott and Cometbus stranded.
years.xp: Per Wikipedia, [[Ben Weasel|bdce6736-8bc6-4818-8fd7-781822b674a9]] of [[Screeching Weasel|e4a135d0-1948-4620-bc07-b0217d09ccc1]] filled in for two shows, then Paul Curran took over and finished the tour, staying to the end of the band.

years.h: Paul Curran joins and finishes the tour
years.p: Paul Curran steps in after the Florida walkout and stays through Crimpshrine's final recordings.

eras.title: Last records, last shows
eras.text: The final year produced a German album, two splits and one last EP before the band ended in May.

years.h: Quit Talkin' Claude... is the last EP
years.p: Crimpshrine's final EP is released shortly before the band ends.

years.h: Lame Gig Contest: released in Germany, not the US
years.p: The album comes out on Musical Tragedies in Germany after Lookout passes on the recordings.
years.xp: Wikipedia's Jeff Ott article says L.A. Weekly named it one of the top five albums of pre-commercial pop punk.

years.h: Two splits: Mutley Chix and G-Whiz
years.p: Crimpshrine appear on split EPs with Mutley Chix (Closed Up, Caught Up and Fucked Up) and G-Whiz (Burning Bridges).
The band splits in May 1989, weeks after Quit Talkin' Claude... came out.
years.xp: Cometbus went on to [[Pinhead Gunpowder|f7b3c394-3654-4bde-baea-32804f87fe24]], Ott to [[Fifteen|51cb9a1a-cc3f-48e6-85c4-b0843fc7b697]], Curran to Monsula and Rypins to Tilt and later the Tantrums.

eras.title: The legacy keeps growing
eras.text: Compilations, a tribute album and a documentary kept the band in view long after the split.

years.h: The Sound of a New World Being Born collects the band
years.p: Lookout gathers Crimpshrine's recordings on a compilation.
Crimpshrine's "Better Half" is paired with [[Jawbreaker|ec88cdc3-0517-4951-b5ef-7323e7316db0]]'s "Sanctuary" on a split 7-inch.

years.h: Tribute album Can You Spare a Dime?
years.p: A tribute album honors Crimpshrine and Fifteen, Jeff Ott's later band.

years.h: Featured in Turn It Around: The Story of East Bay Punk
years.p: The documentary covers the Gilman scene that Crimpshrine helped shape.
